correctness.rationale: Every subgroup is cyclic-Singer or a split order-three extension; the genuine graph orbit counts follow from Burnside, trace-zero difference set and a complete q mod3 calculation. Geometric fixed graphs follow from normal-basis Frobenius Jordan and semisimple decompositions; no edge inversion is possible as bipartition shores are preserved. Exact field-and-quotient orbit enumeration checks ten q including composite prime powers and every index, without using finite testing as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full primary texts on Singer flat orbits (Drudge), projective-plane dessin quotients (Streit–Wolfart), and Frobenius-compatible dessins (Sarti) were compared at the statement-and-implication level. The full Singer quotient graph is already covered and not independently claimed; the new subject is all subgroup quotient homotopy ranks together with geometric fixed-graph classification of all semilinear lifts, including the mod-three arithmetic transition. Related accessible claim records treat different complexes or higher-rank Singer-only quotients. One normalizer paper full text was inaccessible and is a genuine residual priority risk.

value.rationale: A complete homotopy and fixed-point classification for every subgroup of the natural Singer–Frobenius group on Desarguesian projective-plane buildings identifies a sharp q mod3 geometric trichotomy. Distinguishing fixed hexagons, intervals, two-component loci and empty loci is structurally informative beyond the previously known full Singer quotient numerical count.
